brand.name: PostHog
brand.voice: Direct, developer-first, a little irreverent. No buzzwords. Confident without bragging.

product.name: PostHog
hero_features: Free up to 1M events per month

icps.label: Early-stage Startup CTO
pain_points: Stitching together five analytics tools for a team that should be shipping product
Monthly bills from Mixpanel + LogRocket + LaunchDarkly + Hotjar add up before revenue does
Every new tool is another integration, another SDK, another source of truth
No engineering time to maintain a sprawling analytics stack
icps.platform_rationale: Early-stage founders live on LinkedIn for fundraising and hiring — it's where they see B2B tool ads in a professional mindset.

copy.headline:
Every tool a
growing product team needs.
One platform.
copy.subline: PostHog is an open-source product analytics platform that bundles event tracking, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, and surveys into a single stack. Built for founders who'd rather ship than stitch five tools together. Free up to 1M events per month.

visual_treatment.background_mood: A warm cream canvas (#F5F1E8) — almost a plain wash of color. A very gentle, soft radial glow of PostHog orange (#F54E00) anchored in the top-right corner, fading outward and never reaching the center of the frame. The middle of the image is nearly uniform cream, quiet and empty. Feels like premium warm paper. No objects, no text, no patterns. The vibe is founder-friendly, inviting, confident.

icps.label: Engineering Lead / Principal Engineer
pain_points: Can't run SQL against their own product event data — locked behind a SaaS UI
Privacy and compliance requirements make sending user events to a third-party a risk
Vendor lock-in and unpredictable pricing at enterprise scale
Wants analytics owned and operated by engineering, not marketing
icps.platform_rationale: Engineering leads evaluating infra-level tools read HN and technical Twitter. They respond to open-source credibility and self-host options — not to growth-marketing voice.

copy.headline:
Product analytics
you can self-host.
copy.subline: PostHog is open-source and runs on your own infrastructure. Query every event with SQL, keep customer data inside your perimeter, and avoid the vendor lock-in that comes with Mixpanel or Amplitude. Used by teams at Airbus, Hasura, and Y Combinator startups.

visual_treatment.background_mood: A deep slate canvas (#1D1F27) — nearly uniform, with a very soft radial wash of PostHog orange (#F54E00) anchored in the bottom-left corner, bleeding faintly into the frame and stopping well before the center. The middle is quiet, dark, confident. No objects, no patterns, no shapes. Feels like a premium technical product marketing background — serious, sophisticated, engineer-first. No grids, no code, no circuit lines.

icps.label: Growth PM
pain_points: Every experiment lives across three tools — flag system, analytics, session replay
Launch-to-learn cycle is slow because tools don't share a data model
Hard to prove impact of a test when the funnel lives in a different product than the replay
Spends more time plumbing dashboards than reading them
icps.platform_rationale: Growth PMs are on LinkedIn reading product posts and case studies, in a work mindset, receptive to tool-consolidation pitches and outcome framing.

copy.headline:
Launch the test.
Watch the replay.
Read the results.
copy.subline: PostHog bundles feature flags, A/B testing, funnels, and session replay into one platform, so growth teams can ship an experiment and see exactly what happened without leaving the tool. The launch-to-learn loop gets shorter when the data lives in one place.

visual_treatment.background_mood: A soft off-white canvas (#EEEFE7) with a very gentle radial bloom of PostHog orange (#F54E00) anchored in the top-left corner — barely there, fading before it reaches the center. The middle is nearly a flat wash of light cream. Minimal, bright, slightly energetic but still quiet. No objects, no charts, no icons, no patterns. Feels like a clean design studio wall.

icps.label: Indie Hacker / Solo Founder
pain_points: Can't afford enterprise analytics on a bootstrapped budget
Google Analytics is built for marketing sites, not product usage
Needs to see actual user behavior to figure out why people churn
Wants to set up analytics in an evening, not a sprint
icps.platform_rationale: Indie hackers live on Twitter and Indie Hackers — they find tools through peer recommendations and cost-conscious, dev-friendly messaging beats enterprise framing.

copy.headline:
See what your users
actually do in your app.
copy.subline: PostHog records every click, scroll, rage-click, and drop-off with session replay, event tracking, and funnels in one tool. Free up to 1M events per month, no credit card required. Set up in about ten minutes.

visual_treatment.background_mood: A warm peach-cream canvas (#F9EFE3) — almost a flat wash of color. A very faint radial glow of PostHog orange (#F54E00) anchored in the bottom-right corner, drifting inward softly and stopping before the center. The middle of the frame is quiet and uniform. Inviting, approachable, a little homey — like a cozy workshop wall. No objects, no people, no patterns, no shapes.
